gaps.sentence: She ___ her breath before diving into the pool.
gaps.explanation: 'Hold one's breath' — catching breath is recovering it afterwards.

gaps.sentence: She has ___ a diary since she was twelve.
gaps.explanation: keep a diary is the fixed collocation for writing in one regularly.

gaps.sentence: We are still ___ arrangements for the wedding.
gaps.explanation: make arrangements is the fixed collocation for organising plans.

gaps.sentence: Do you want a ___ cup of tea or a weak one?
gaps.explanation: strong tea/coffee means made with a lot of tea leaves or coffee; its opposite is weak.

gaps.sentence: A true friend will always ___ a secret.
gaps.explanation: keep a secret is the fixed collocation for not telling it to anyone.

gaps.sentence: Her company ___ a huge profit last year.
gaps.explanation: make a profit (or make a loss) is the fixed business collocation.

gaps.sentence: It took her years to ___ a living from her painting.
gaps.explanation: make a living means to earn enough money to live on.

gaps.sentence: I ___ hours yesterday trying to fix the printer, and it still doesn't work.
gaps.hint: fixed phrase: to use time without any result
gaps.explanation: waste time means to spend time uselessly; the second clause shows there was no result.
